external_entities.name: developers
external_entities.description: People who push branches and can log in to the build runner to initiate rebuilds.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: Internet-hosted registry reached during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Picks up merges, fetches source, resolves the dependency lockfile, produces container images, pushes images, calls the deploy controller, and can be used to initiate manual rebuilds.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: Receives release requests and serves the current release to store servers.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small server in each store's back office running the till software as a container; polls for the current release, pulls changed images, and restarts the container.
processes.source_excerpt: Each store has a small server in the back office running the till software as a container.
processes.notes: Represents the store-server role across about 1,200 stores.

data_stores.name: git server
data_stores.description: Self-hosted repository on the corporate network containing developer branches and the source used for builds.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the git server encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: Registry in the build environment containing finished container images tagged with commit SHAs.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: release record
data_stores.description: The record held by the deploy controller identifying which image SHA the estate should run.
data_stores.source_excerpt: holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: Developers push branches to the self-hosted git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: merge main
data_flows.description: A merge to main starts a build.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A merge to `main` is what starts a build.

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner fetches source from the git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reaches out to the public package registry while resolving dependencies.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.

data_flows.name: publish image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes the finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.notes: Images are tagged with the commit sha.

data_flows.name: set current release
data_flows.description: The build runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When the image is pushed the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release.
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.

data_flows.name: check release
data_flows.description: Each store server asks the deploy controller for the current release once a minute.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current image from the registry when its running image differs.
data_flows.source_excerpt: if it differs from what it is running it pulls that image from the registry
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.

data_flows.name: rebuild main
data_flows.description: A developer can log in to the build runner and manually kick off a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The network on which the self-hosted git server and deploy controller run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: The separate environment containing the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The network zone containing the store servers across the in-store estate.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet reached for dependency resolution.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet

assumptions.assumption: The git server's source and branches are business-critical operating data.
assumptions.basis: The store contains developer branches and source used by the build pipeline.

assumptions.assumption: The git server's contents are confidential because they are source code for the build and deploy system.
assumptions.basis: The store contains source code and dependency information for the system.

assumptions.assumption: The image registry's container images are business-critical operating data.
assumptions.basis: The registry stores finished images that are deployed to the store estate.

assumptions.assumption: The image registry's contents are confidential because they are deployment images for the till software.
assumptions.basis: The store contains the finished container image used by the estate.

assumptions.assumption: The release record is business-critical operating data.
assumptions.basis: It records which image SHA the estate should run.

assumptions.assumption: The release record is confidential because it controls the estate's current software release.
assumptions.basis: The record identifies the image SHA that the store estate should be on.

assumptions.assumption: The build runner handles business-critical build and deployment data.
assumptions.basis: It fetches source, produces container images, and initiates deployment.

assumptions.assumption: The build runner handles credentials.
assumptions.basis: It uses a shared build token to call the deploy controller.

assumptions.assumption: The deploy controller handles business-critical release data.
assumptions.basis: It holds and serves the release record for the store estate.

assumptions.assumption: The store server handles business-critical deployment data.
assumptions.basis: It checks the current release and pulls the image it is to run.

assumptions.assumption: The developers present business-critical source and branch data.
assumptions.basis: They push branches and source changes into the build pipeline.

assumptions.assumption: The branch-push flow carries business-critical source changes.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries developer branches and source changes.

assumptions.assumption: The merge flow carries business-critical build input.
assumptions.basis: The merge to main starts a build.

assumptions.assumption: The source-fetch flow carries business-critical source and dependency data.
assumptions.basis: The runner fetches source and the dependency lockfile.

assumptions.assumption: The dependency-resolution flow carries business-critical build dependency data.
assumptions.basis: The runner downloads dependencies used to produce the container image.

assumptions.assumption: The image-publish flow carries business-critical deployment data.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries the finished container image deployed to stores.

assumptions.assumption: The release-request flow carries business-critical release data and credentials.
assumptions.basis: It carries the image SHA and uses the shared build token.

assumptions.assumption: The release-check flow carries business-critical release data.
assumptions.basis: It requests the current release image SHA.

assumptions.assumption: The image-pull flow carries business-critical deployment data.
assumptions.basis: It carries the container image to the store server.

assumptions.assumption: The manual-rebuild flow carries business-critical build data and credentials.
assumptions.basis: A developer logs in and initiates a rebuild of main.
